powerveyra.headline: Clarity for complex energy data.
powerveyra.intro: PowerVeyra brings structure to power-plant reporting: importing records, retaining their origins, and making historical measurements easier to inspect and understand.
powerveyra.problem: Operational reports can be difficult to reconcile, explore and explain when their readings are spread across files. An attractive chart is only useful when its underlying source can be understood.
powerveyra.approach: A local reporting application connects retained report files to structured readings and bilingual visualizations. Data-quality and source checks make uncertainty visible alongside the information itself.
details: Persistent report imports with source traceability.
Historical chart exploration and bilingual explanations.
Review workflows for report revisions and archive integrity.
A telemetry receiving contract developed separately from historical reporting.
powerveyra.boundary: A private application in development. Historical analytics and a receiving API do not establish a commissioned live SCADA connection, equipment control or certified sensor accuracy.
powerveyra.takeaway: Trust belongs in the data model, not just in the dashboard.

walsong-fit.headline: A calmer way to track progress.
walsong-fit.intro: Walsong Fit brings training, nutrition, recovery and everyday progress into a phone-first personal performance application.
walsong-fit.problem: Personal tracking becomes a chore when everyday records live in separate places. The product explores a clearer connection between the actions someone records and the progress they can understand.
walsong-fit.approach: A responsive web application combines workout and nutrition workflows with owner-scoped records and shared domain calculations. An early native client extends the product in deliberate, testable slices.
details: Workout plans, sets, rest timers and training history.
Manual nutrition, reusable meals, hydration and recovery records.
Progress views, data exports and offline workout-set drafts.
Early native development with shared models and selected testing workflows.
walsong-fit.boundary: A private pre-release with web and early native development. A full native release, wearable integration and AI food analysis are not claimed as available features.
walsong-fit.takeaway: Useful tracking starts with records people can understand and control.

batolekha.headline: Local context. Thoughtful journeys.
batolekha.intro: BatoLekha is a Nepal-focused tourism platform exploring two connected needs: useful traveler discovery and structured trip operations for trekking and adventure agencies.
batolekha.problem: Travel ideas and agency operations need different kinds of information. Combining them responsibly requires clear boundaries between public editorial content and protected business records.
batolekha.approach: The traveler experience supports destination discovery and temporary planning. A separate protected workspace organizes agency trip records, with source-aware content and explicit distinctions between ideas and verified information.
details: Destination discovery with search, area and travel-style filters.
Temporary trip planning and source-aware journey information.
Protected agency workspaces and trip lifecycle records.
Responsive web foundations and an early mobile source prototype.
batolekha.boundary: In development. Discovery and planning do not imply live bookings, payment processing, verified trail navigation or a released native application.
batolekha.takeaway: A good travel product is clear about what it knows—and what it does not.

abroadmitra.headline: Better context for a big decision.
abroadmitra.intro: AbroadMitra helps students explore universities and study-abroad options through organized information and explainable recommendations.
abroadmitra.problem: Comparing study options means balancing location, budget, academic background and course interests. A useful recommendation should make its reasons visible.
abroadmitra.approach: A React interface works with a layered .NET API and a structured data model. The reviewed recommendation service filters candidates and scores explicit criteria, returning reasons alongside the results.
details: University and course discovery backed by a structured API.
Budget and destination filtering before recommendation scoring.
Weighted matching with explanations for individual results.
Recommendation-service tests covering filtering and scoring behavior.
abroadmitra.boundary: An implemented software project. The reviewed recommendation engine is rule-based; matches are decision support, not admission predictions or guarantees. A current public demo is not verified.
abroadmitra.takeaway: Recommendations earn trust when their reasoning is visible.

nepalkhata.headline: Practical software for the shop floor.
nepalkhata.intro: NepalKhata is a desktop hardware-shop management project for inventory, invoicing, customers and suppliers, with optional AI-assisted product search.
nepalkhata.problem: Shop software needs to make stock and billing reliable without making basic operations depend on an internet connection.
nepalkhata.approach: A .NET/WPF application separates interface, business concerns and SQLite data access. The reviewed invoice flow uses a transaction to record invoice items and update stock together.
details: Inventory, customer and supplier management.
Invoice and stock updates within a database transaction.
Local SQLite storage with a Dapper data layer.
Optional Claude-powered search and an MVVM desktop interface.
nepalkhata.boundary: Implementation is present in the public repository. This portfolio does not establish customer adoption, current production deployment or independent billing-compliance certification.
nepalkhata.takeaway: The best business tools fit the conditions where the business actually runs.

jwelflow.headline: Software that understands the trade.
jwelflow.intro: Walsong JwelFlow explores the specific workflows of jewelry retailers in Nepal, from inventory and billing to artisan work and local weight calculations.
jwelflow.problem: Jewelry retail has domain details that general inventory software can miss: traditional weight units, material rates, making charges and specialist workflows.
jwelflow.approach: A Next.js application and Tauri desktop wrapper use local RxDB storage. A dedicated calculation module handles weight conversion and decimal-based price arithmetic.
details: Jewelry inventory and point-of-sale interfaces.
Tola, masha and lal conversion with decimal arithmetic.
Artisan-work and customer workflow modules.
Local database collections and schema-migration code.
jwelflow.boundary: An implemented project requiring further release validation. No claim of certified legal compliance, encrypted backup or guaranteed data-loss prevention is made.
jwelflow.takeaway: Domain understanding is an engineering feature.

documind.eyebrow: ANSWERS WITH A WAY BACK TO THE SOURCE
documind.headline: Look inside the answer.
documind.intro: DocuMind is a document-question-answering API prototype that combines local embeddings, vector retrieval and language-model generation with source attribution.
documind.problem: A document answer is hard to evaluate without seeing the passages that informed it. The prototype makes retrieval evidence part of the response.
documind.approach: FastAPI coordinates PDF parsing, overlapping text chunks, local sentence embeddings and a FAISS index. Retrieved passages form the prompt context, and the response includes source pages and similarity scores.
details: PDF upload, parsing and overlapping text chunks.
Local embeddings and normalized-vector similarity retrieval.
Groq-backed answer generation from retrieved context.
Source passages and page references returned through the API.
documind.boundary: An API prototype. The reviewed implementation is not a production multi-user document service; the larger UI, routing and agent roadmap is separate from the available code.
documind.takeaway: Source attribution is part of the experience, not an afterthought.
